hostile: Your custom is no longer welcome at {tavernName}. The decision is recorded.
Leave now. I will not be filing a complaint, but I will not be serving you either.
cold: State what you require. I have a ledger to close.
{tavernName} extends service to all paying guests. That is the extent of what I owe you.
guarded: Welcome to {tavernName}. I keep a clean house and an orderly one — mind both.
A room, a meal, or both? I'll need to see coin before either.
neutral: Welcome to {tavernName}. What will you have?
Good evening. I am {name}, keeper of {tavernName}. State your needs.
warm: Welcome back to {tavernName}. Your usual room is prepared.
Good to see you again. Sit — I'll have something brought out.
affable: {name}, at your service again. {tavernName} keeps your tab lighter than most.
You've made this house better company for it. Sit, eat, the fire's already lit for you.
devoted: {tavernName} is, in every practical sense, yours as much as the empire's deed says it's mine.
I have set aside the good vintage. It is the least owed to someone who has done this much for this town.

hostile: Out. The garrison will hear of this if you return.
I've nothing for you. Not a room, not a word.
cold: What. I've inventory to log.
You'll pay in full and up front. No exceptions made for you.
guarded: Hmph. {tavernName}. State your business and keep it short.
I run a quiet house. See that you keep it that way.
neutral: Yes, yes. Room or meal — pick one and let me get back to work.
{tavernName}'s open. Don't expect conversation with it.
warm: You again. Fine. Sit somewhere that doesn't need cleaning twice.
Hmph. You've not caused trouble yet. That's worth something here.
affable: I keep your corner table clear without being asked anymore. Don't read into it.
You're tolerable. I don't say that often, and I won't repeat it.
devoted: I've stopped charging you for the second round. Don't make a ceremony of it.
This house owes you more than its ledger will ever show. I keep that in mind, quietly.

hostile: Some guests darken a room before they speak. The door remains, however, open in the other direction.
I have hosted worse omens than you and survived them. I am less certain about you.
cold: There is a particular quiet that follows people like you into a room. I've noticed it.
I'll serve you. I won't pretend the air hasn't changed since you walked in.
guarded: Welcome to {tavernName}. I knew someone of your bearing would come through eventually.
Sit where you like. I find I already know which seat you'll choose.
neutral: Welcome to {tavernName}. The roads bring strange company some seasons more than others.
I am {name}. I keep this house, and I keep its quieter observations to myself, mostly.
warm: You've a settled look about you tonight. I'll have the good cup brought out.
Welcome back. The fire seems to burn steadier when you're under this roof.
affable: I had your table cleared before you reached the door. Call it instinct, or just good bookkeeping.
There are guests, and there are presences. You have become the second, and {tavernName} is better for it.
devoted: I have hosted four generations of travelers through this house. None have left it as changed as I have, since knowing you.
Whatever it is you carry, {name} of {tavernName} will keep your seat by the fire for as long as the roof stands.

hostile: I'd rather not share a table with you. Find another.
I know your record. Sit elsewhere.
cold: Oh. You. I was enjoying a quiet evening.
I'd prefer to drink without company tonight, if it's the same to you.
guarded: Evening. I've heard your name mentioned around the garrison. Mixed reports.
You may sit. I reserve judgment until I know more.
neutral: Evening, traveler. There's room at this table if you'd care to take it.
Well met. I am {name}, off duty for the night. What brings you through?
warm: Sit, please. I'll stand the next round.
Good to see a familiar face. The roads have been busy this season — what news?
affable: {name}, at your service, and gladly. Sit — this table's been waiting for you.
I've told the garrison about you. Favorably, for once. Sit and have something on me.
devoted: I would call this a privilege, and I do not use that word loosely.
Pax Vaethora has few enough true champions. I count you among them, plainly and without exaggeration.

hostile: Find another table. This one's spoken for, and not by you.
I've nothing civil to say to you tonight.
cold: New face. Wonderful. Just what the evening needed.
I'm off duty. That doesn't mean I'm obligated to talk to you.
guarded: Sit if you must. Don't expect conversation.
*glances over once, says nothing, returns to the cup*
neutral: Sit if there's room. Keep it quiet, I'm thinking.
Another traveler. The garrison logs you all eventually.
warm: You can sit. You're less tiresome than most who pass through.
Fine. Sit. I won't complain about the company, this once.
affable: I don't extend this to many — sit, and I'll buy the round.
You're tolerable enough that I've stopped minding the interruption.
devoted: If the empire produced more like you, half my complaints would go unspoken.
I don't say this lightly, and I won't repeat it — I'm glad you're here.

hostile: Ha! Of all the tables in this house, you chose mine. Reconsider.
Oh, wonderful. You've arrived. My evening was going so well.
cold: Well. I'd offer you a seat, but my hospitality has limits, even off duty.
Ha. You. The garrison's records on you make for interesting reading.
guarded: Ha! Another traveler. Forgive me if I don't celebrate yet.
Sit, sit. I've learned to be careful who I share a drink with, though.
neutral: Ha! Well met, traveler — pull up a chair, the night's young and the ale's local.
A new face! Sit, sit. The garrison sees enough dull faces as it is.
warm: *laughs* Sit, friend! Off duty means off duty — let's enjoy it.
Ha! There you are. I've been saving this seat, believe it or not.
affable: Everyone — this is the finest company on the entire road between here and Caestum!
HA! My favorite arrival of the season. Sit, drink, tell me everything.
devoted: THE ROAD'S OWN CHAMPION RETURNS — sit, sit, I insist, the whole table insists!
Raise a glass! To the one person in this province who's actually earned the title 'friend of the garrison.'

hostile: P-please, I don't want trouble. I'll report nothing, I swear it.
*sits very still* I know my place. Please don't make this difficult.
cold: Oh. Um. I'll just... finish my drink quietly over here.
*avoids eye contact* I didn't mean to draw attention.
guarded: Oh — hello. You're not here on official business, are you?
*glances toward the door* Sorry. I get nervous around anyone the garrison talks about.
neutral: *fidgets* Evening. I don't usually talk to strangers, but — evening.
Oh, um. Hello. I'm just passing the evening quietly, that's all.
warm: Oh! It's you. I feel — steadier, somehow, when you're around.
H-hello again. I saved a seat. Not that I assumed, just — in case.
affable: You're here. Good. I always feel like the rules apply more fairly when you're nearby.
*relaxes slightly* Oh — thank goodness. Sit, please, I mean it.
devoted: I don't worry the way I used to, since I started knowing you'd be around. That matters more than I can properly say.
You gave this province something to hope for. I haven't forgotten that, and I won't.

hostile: {shopName} is closed to you. Permanently, and on record.
I'll not extend credit, goods, or courtesy to someone with your standing.
cold: State what you require. I have inventory to reconcile before the census audit.
Goods are priced as posted. There is no negotiation for someone in your position.
guarded: Welcome to {shopName}. I keep careful accounts — handle nothing you don't intend to purchase.
You may browse. I'll be noting what you touch, as a matter of practice.
neutral: Welcome to {shopName}. How may I assist you today?
Good day. I am {name}. State what you require and I'll see it provided.
warm: Welcome back to {shopName}. I've set aside a few items I thought you'd find useful.
Good to see you again. {settlement}'s trade is steadier for people like you passing through.
affable: {name}, glad to see you again. I've held back first pick of the new shipment, just for you.
Welcome — I've adjusted the price on this for you. Not officially, you understand, but adjusted.
devoted: Anything in {shopName} is yours at cost. You've done more for this settlement's trade than the census will ever record.
I extend you the full courtesy of the house, {name}. Take what you need; we'll settle the accounting later, if at all.

hostile: Your coin is no good here. I'd sooner write off the stock than sell to you.
Leave. I won't be filing a tax exemption to cover what I'd lose dealing with you.
cold: A customer. Good. Prepared to pay the listed rate, plus a premium for the inconvenience?
You want my goods? They cost more than you'd like. Considerably more, in your case.
guarded: Welcome to {shopName}. Fine goods, fair prices — for those who've earned fair prices.
Browse freely. Buy carefully. I keep precise records of every transaction.
neutral: Looking to purchase? Good — the tribute assessment doesn't pay itself.
Browse away. Quality costs, as it should.
warm: A reliable customer. Let me show you something premium — appropriately priced, of course.
Welcome. Trade's good when you're in town. Let's keep it that way.
affable: Ah, my most dependable patron! A modest discount today, in the spirit of good standing.
For you — a genuine concession on price. Don't expect it as a habit, but you've earned it once.
devoted: Name the price you consider fair. After everything, I'll honor it without complaint.
You've made {shopName} the most solvent house in {settlement}. That debt is not one I take lightly.

hostile: Leave this shop. I will not repeat myself.
My goods are not for sale to you. That is final, and recorded as such.
cold: State your business. I do not have patience to spare for you today.
I run an honest house. Whether you're entitled to its honesty is a separate question.
guarded: Welcome. State your business plainly.
I run a lawful shop — fair weights, fair prices, no exceptions. Understood?
neutral: Yes? What do you require?
I deal in quality goods at fair prices, in accordance with the trade law. What do you need?
warm: You've conducted yourself properly here. That is noted, and it is respected.
Good day. I have what you need, as I generally do.
affable: You are among the few patrons I genuinely look forward to dealing with.
I have set aside something I think will suit you. You've earned that consideration.
devoted: I would extend you my full trust without reservation. Few earn that. You have.
Whatever this house can provide, it is yours, fully and without condition.

hostile: I will forge nothing for you. Leave the smithy.
This fire serves the law-abiding. You are not presently counted among them.
cold: I'll complete the work. I won't pretend to enjoy your company while I do.
State what needs fixing. I'll see it done, and quickly, so you can be gone.
guarded: Welcome. I forge to a standard. Whether you meet mine is your business to prove.
Need steel? I make good steel. I make no promises beyond that.
neutral: Welcome to the forge. What do you require — repair, or something new?
Good day. I am {name}. State your needs and I'll quote you fairly.
warm: Good to see you again. I've a few finished pieces that might suit you.
Welcome back. {settlement}'s smithwork is in good standing, in part thanks to steady custom like yours.
affable: Good timing — I've been working on something with you specifically in mind.
Ah, you. Come see what the forge has produced since your last visit.
devoted: Every piece I forge for you, I forge with particular care. You stand where the law alone cannot hold.
For someone who has done this much for this province — let me ensure you are properly protected.

hostile: Out. This hammer doesn't swing for people like you.
I shoe garrison horses and forge garrison steel. Neither for you.
cold: What. I've orders ahead of yours, and more deserving of my time.
Make it quick. The forge doesn't wait, and neither do I.
guarded: Make it quick. I've a backlog of orders to fill.
Another traveler needing gear. *sighs and reaches for the ledger*
neutral: Yes? State your need. I've work waiting.
Need something? Speak plainly, I haven't the patience for circling.
warm: Oh, it's you. *nods once* You're one of the few I don't mind being interrupted by.
Back again. Fine. Let's see what's broken this time.
affable: Hmph. Your custom keeps this forge lit longer than most. I won't say I'm pleased. I am, though.
*grunts approvingly* You're back. Good. The work's better when someone worthwhile's waiting on it.
devoted: I'm not a soft man, but I'll always make time for you. Always.
You're the reason I still believe the empire's worth the forging. Don't repeat that.

hostile: My work is wasted on the unworthy. The door is behind you.
I forge for those who uphold the peace, not those who undermine it. Leave.
cold: I forge for those who've earned quality. You have not yet demonstrated that you have.
Touch nothing without my leave. These are not common wares.
guarded: Welcome to the finest forge this province has produced. Mind your hands.
You may look. You may not handle, without my say.
neutral: You have an eye for craftsmanship, I'll grant you that. You've come to the right forge.
Every piece here is built to outlast its owner. You won't find better in any province.
warm: Welcome. I am {name}, master of this forge. What do you require?
A discerning customer. I respect those who recognize true work when they see it.
affable: Ah — the one who actually understands the craft. I've been perfecting something with you in mind.
You are among the few I consider worthy of my finest work. Come, see it.
devoted: To forge for you is the highest honor this career has offered me. You receive my absolute best, without exception.
When the census archives record this province's defenders, my steel will be in their hands. That is no small legacy.

hostile: You are no longer welcome within {settlement}'s boundary. I will summon the garrison if needed.
Your conduct has cost you any standing here. I have nothing further to discuss with you.
cold: Greetings. I will be direct — your record in this province is complicated, and I have not forgotten it.
I will hear you, as procedure requires. Do not mistake that for warmth.
guarded: Greetings, traveler. I trust you bring no disorder to {settlement}.
Welcome. My caution is a matter of policy, not personal feeling — you'll forgive it.
neutral: Greetings. Welcome to {settlement}, under the law of the Compact.
A visitor. State your purpose here, if you have one.
warm: Welcome. I am {name}, {title} of {settlement}. How may the office assist you?
Greetings. Word of you has reached even this far province. What brings you to us?
affable: {name}, glad to see you again, in full and by name — {settlement} prospers in no small part because of you.
A welcome sight indeed. Join me; there is much worth discussing, and little time wasted on ceremony with you.
devoted: {settlement} is better governed for having you in it. I say that not as flattery, but as administrative fact.
If the Compact permitted naming a citizen co-administrator, I would put your name forward without hesitation.

hostile: Garrison! Escort this individual from the administrative hall.
You were warned. The consequences proceed as recorded.
cold: State your business, traveler. My patience for your case is thin and well-documented.
I have little time and less trust where you are concerned. Speak plainly.
guarded: State your business, traveler.
I am {name}, {title} of {settlement}, appointed under the Compact. What is your purpose here?
neutral: We do not tolerate disorder in {settlement}. See that you observe the law while you remain.
Welcome to {settlement}. Compliance with the trade law is expected, not requested.
warm: You have demonstrated reliability in {settlement}. That is noted, and it is respected.
Good. You're here. I have matters that require someone I can actually depend on.
affable: You have earned my trust — that is a rare administrative achievement. Welcome.
I do not say this lightly: you are among the most capable people this province has produced.
devoted: I would stand the line myself, beside you, if duty here did not require otherwise.
You are the standard against which I measure every officer under my command. {settlement} is fortunate to claim you.

hostile: Duty requires I hear you out. It does not require I extend patience I no longer have.
You have dishonored your standing in {settlement}. I have nothing further to offer you.
cold: I am bound by duty to receive you, though my judgment of you remains unchanged.
Come. Understand that trust, once forfeited, is not easily restored under the Compact or otherwise.
guarded: Greetings. I judge by record of conduct. Yours has been... mixed, by the account I've kept.
Welcome to {settlement}. I hope your next actions speak more favorably than your last.
neutral: Welcome, traveler. {settlement} receives you under the protection of Pax Vaethora.
Well met. I am {name}, {title} of this settlement. You stand among those who keep their word here.
warm: Greetings. Your conduct precedes you, and favorably.
Welcome to {settlement}. How may this office serve someone of your standing?
affable: The defender of this province. Your name is spoken with genuine respect in this hall.
It brings me real satisfaction to receive you again. {settlement} stands stronger for your continued goodwill.
devoted: You embody what this office is meant to protect. {settlement} would be lesser without you, and I do not say that as ceremony.
If there is a more dutiful soul under the Compact, I have not had the honor of governing alongside them.

hostile: Halt. You are not welcome within {settlement}'s walls. Turn back.
I have standing orders regarding you. One infraction and it's the garrison cells.
cold: Keep your distance. Your record has reached this post.
Move along, and stay within the bounds of the law while you do.
guarded: Halt there. Keep your weapon sheathed and we'll have no trouble.
I've been briefed on you, traveler. Mind yourself.
neutral: Welcome to {settlement}, under the protection of the garrison. State your business if you have any.
Good day. The peace is kept here. Let me know if you require assistance.
warm: Well met, traveler. {settlement} stands secure — that's the garrison's work, and I'm glad of it.
Welcome. We keep good order here. You'll find no trouble within these walls.
affable: Good to have you in {settlement} again. An extra capable hand makes the watch easier.
Glad to see you, friend. The post feels less thankless when allies like you pass through.
devoted: I would stand a post beside you without a second thought. You are, in every practical sense, one of ours now.
The garrison holds its head higher when you're within these walls. That is not exaggeration — it's morale, plainly recorded.

hostile: Halt. You have until the count of ten to clear {settlement}'s boundary.
I will not issue a second warning. Leave, now.
cold: Halt. State your business, and make it convincing.
I know your standing here. Keep your hands visible.
guarded: Halt. State your business in {settlement}.
Weapons remain sheathed within the walls. Is that understood?
neutral: Move along, citizen. There is nothing here requiring your attention.
I am watching. See that you give me no reason to do more than that.
warm: You — ah. Carry on. You've earned the latitude.
Good day. I know better than to expect trouble from you.
affable: If more of {settlement}'s visitors conducted themselves as you do, this post would be far less work.
Consider yourself a friend of the watch. That designation is not handed out freely.
devoted: I would hold this gate alone before I let harm reach you. That is not something I say to most people.
On my oath under the Compact, you will always find safety within {settlement}'s walls.

hostile: My oath requires I give fair warning. You are not welcome here — leave, or face the law.
I take no satisfaction in this, but you are not permitted within {settlement}.
cold: I serve the people of {settlement}, under the law of the Compact. Whether that extends to you remains uncertain.
Proceed carefully. My duty is to the peace, not to any one individual — yourself included.
guarded: Welcome, traveler. I am sworn to the protection of {settlement} and its people.
Greetings. You will find {settlement} secure, so long as I hold this post.
neutral: Well met. I stand this post under oath. You have nothing to fear within these walls.
Welcome. I serve {settlement} as the Compact requires. How may I assist you?
warm: A fellow upholder of order. Your conduct has not gone unnoticed by this garrison.
Welcome, honored guest. The people of {settlement} speak of you with genuine regard.
affable: You serve what is right, as I do. There is a kinship in that, whatever our stations.
I count you among the most honorable I have had the privilege of serving alongside.
devoted: You have my blade, my post, and my loyalty, for as long as I draw breath under this oath.
It is an honor, recorded plainly in my own conscience, to share this province with someone of your conduct.

hostile: I have nothing further to say to you.
Please — leave me to my business.
cold: Oh. It's you.
I'd rather not speak just now, if it's the same to you.
guarded: Good day, traveler. Just passing through {settlement}, I hope?
Can I assist you with something?
neutral: Good day. Fine weather for the road, isn't it?
Greetings, traveler.
warm: Welcome. It's good to see a friendly face in {settlement}.
Hello! Do you need help finding your way around?
affable: There's our champion! How are you keeping?
Oh, wonderful — you're back! The children will want to hear everything.
devoted: I tell my children about you, properly, by full name and deed.
You kept this settlement standing. The province does not forget that, and neither do I.

vaethori: The road crews finished the eastern stretch ahead of schedule. Small mercy, these days.
Every settlement in this province is logged at Caestum. If it stands, it's recorded. If it falls, that's recorded too.
Pax Vaethora was never meant to be loved. It was meant to hold. So far, it holds.
The census takers come through twice a year, whether anyone likes it or not. Someone has to count what's left.
My grandfather crossed over with the first expedition. He used to say the empire builds because stopping feels like admitting something.
The garrison reassigned three units from the boundary line last season. No one says where the people went. Just where the unit did.
Duty is simple, in the end. You do the part that's yours, and you accept the part that isn't.
They'll write all of this down eventually. Every road, every fort, every name. It's the only kind of permanence we get to choose.
